places.rationale: A huge sovereign fund and tiny citizen base cushion the end of LNG, but consumption across a mostly migrant population, extreme heat, total reliance on desalination and Gulf war risk keep stagnation and decline real.
Fast EU convergence, low debt and good governance make further gains likely; the main tail is Russian aggression on NATO's eastern flank, with very low fertility a slow drag.
Decades of near-flat income per head, very high homicide, import dependence and intensifying Category 5 hurricanes weigh against recent fiscal repair and room to grow.

A very low base and a fragile but working democracy leave room for gains, but four decades of stagnant income per head, fast population growth, Sahel heat and a low-lying capital keep the downside wide.
Declining oil output, heavy debt service, weak governance after the 2023 coup and a half-century of flat income per head cap the upside; ample water and forest are buffers.
Africa's strongest institutions and low debt favour gains, but diamond dependence as lab-grown stones erode demand, severe water stress and rising heat add real stagnation risk.
Very poor, with a heavy HIV burden, weak governance and textile exports hit by US tariffs, and fully tied to South Africa's fortunes; exported highland water is its main durable asset.
The EU accession path offers strong convergence from a modest base, while Russian pressure via Transnistria, energy import dependence and emigration drive the downside.
A credible EU accession track, tourism growth and long life expectancy favour convergence; emigration, summer drought, water stress and middling governance are the drags.
Among the weakest states anywhere, with repeated coups, narco-trafficking, reliance on cashews and a low coast exposed to sea-level rise, so stagnation and collapse carry high weight.
Peaceful, well governed, water-secure and climate-resilient, so the main question is growth speed against fast aging, not catastrophe.
Oil is running out under a kleptocratic regime with almost no readiness to adapt and a looming succession crisis, so decline and collapse are unusually likely despite a small population.
EU and NATO anchoring support convergence, tempered by the Russian border and a large Russian-speaking minority, slower recent growth than its neighbours and steep population aging.
Plenty of room to converge, but a stalled EU path, emigration, rising water stress and weak government effectiveness slow it.
Depleting oil, public debt near 150% of GDP that depends on Gulf bailouts, sectarian instability, extreme water stress and exposure to Iran make it the most fragile of the rich Gulf states.
Stable democracy, ASEAN entry and a low base favour growth, but the fiscal cliff as the petroleum fund drains, high malnutrition and climate exposure pose real downside risk.
A rich EU member near rich-world living standards, but extreme water stress, a hotter and drier eastern Mediterranean, the unresolved division and nearby Middle East wars add tail risk.
Falling gas output in a petrochemical economy, rising debt, very high homicide and instability in neighbouring Venezuela make stagnation or decline about as likely as further gains.
Top-tier governance, very low debt and a digital economy point to strong convergence; the main tail is Russia on its border, plus very low fertility and the oil-shale transition.
An absolute monarchy with recent unrest, a heavy HIV burden and dependence on South African customs revenue and sugar make it fragile, even with a modest income base to grow from.
